## Understanding

<!-- STATE_BLOCK:UNDERSTANDING:BEGIN -->
<!-- MUTABLE | owner: orchestrator | populated-at: Phase 1 -->

### Requirements Summary
Create a /scope-creep slash command workflow that allows injecting additional work into an active feature or bugfix workflow at any point during execution. The workflow:
- Accepts a plain-text description of additional work (not a JIRA ticket)
- Is always received by the orchestrator regardless of which agents were working
- Follows a shortened version of feature/bugfix (no bootstrap, no branch/PR creation)
- Updates all state records (PR body + state file) as if the work was originally planned
- Uses the same agent set (planner-lite, coder, etc.)
- Should avoid significant diversion from existing plans

Acceptance criteria:
1. During a feature workflow, /scope-creep adds a new task and updates plan, state, PR correctly
2. Same for bugfix workflow

### Key Constraints
- Must work with both feature and bugfix workflows (invoked mid-execution)
- No new agents or skills required
- No refactoring of existing workflow files
- Plan approval required per ticket

### Key Files and Patterns Discovered
- canonical/workflows/feature.md - Full feature workflow with STEP-X.Y numbering, 6 phases
- canonical/workflows/bugfix.md - Full bugfix workflow, 7 phases
- canonical/workflows/_resume.md - Shared resume procedure
- canonical/prompts/_registry.yaml - YAML registry with slug, description, agent, argument_hint
- canonical/prompts/feature.md - Simple prompt referencing agent-workflows/feature.md
- canonical/agents/orchestrator.md - Has Input Routing and Workflow Types tables
- README.md - Documents features, workflows, slash commands
- Workflow files use {{VAR}} template variables (PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS_FILE, AGENTS_DIR, TASK_TRACKING_INSTRUCTION, TASK_COMPLETION_INSTRUCTION)

### Build / Test / Lint Commands
- python -m pytest tests/
- python scripts/assemble.py --target-dir examples-autogenerated/vscode-copilot --platform copilot
- python scripts/assemble.py --target-dir examples-autogenerated/vscode-copilot --platform copilot --check

### Open Questions
- None
